algorithms.name: PSIPS (PSI with Posterior Sampling)
requires_knowledge_of: S (bound L_Theta on Theta, transductive linear)

conditions: algorithm is delta-correct on all problems in D^K

source.label: lem:lower_bound
source.quote: An algorithm which is $\delta$-correct on all problems in $\cD^K$ satisfies that, for all $\bm{\nu} \in \cD^K$ with regression matrix $\bm \theta \in \Theta$, $\bE_{\bm\nu}[\tau_{\delta}] \ge T^\star(\bm \theta) \log(1/(2.4\delta))$ where $T^\star(\bm \theta)$ is a characteristic time whose inverse is defined as $2T^\star(\bm \theta)^{-1} \eqdef \sup_{\bm w} \inf_{\bm \lambda \in \Theta \cap \alt (S^\star(\bm \theta))} \|\vv(\bm \theta - \bm \lambda)\|^2_{\Sigma^{-1} \otimes V_{\bm w}}$

results.notes: Stated for general Theta; recorded here for the unstructured case. The proof follows Garivier & Kaufmann (2016); T_star is the PSI characteristic time.

results.notes: Same lemma, recorded for the transductive linear setting. T_star is defined with the inf over Theta ∩ Alt.

source.label: lem:delta_correctness
source.quote: Regardless of the sampling rule, the PS stopping rule with $c(t,\delta) = \beta(t,\frac{\delta}{2})/\log \frac{1}{\delta}$ and $M(t,\delta) = \left\lceil \frac{\log(2 t^s \zeta(s) /\delta)}{\delta q(t,\delta)} \right\rceil $ ensures that the algorithm is $\delta$-correct for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, \textbf{1)} when $\Theta = \bR^{K \times d}$, $\cZ = \cA$, $h = K$, $\bm A = I_{K}$ ...

results.notes: This is δ-correctness of the posterior-sampling (PS) stopping rule, which holds for any sampling rule.

tuning: M(t,delta) as in Lemma 1 with q(t,delta) = r(delta,1)
results.notes: This is δ-correctness of the PS stopping rule, which holds for any sampling rule.

AdaHedge max learner, PS min learner

source.label: thm:asymptotic_upper_bound_sample
source.quote: Using budget $M$ and inflation $c$ such that $\limsup_{\delta \to 0} \frac{c(t, \delta) \log M(t, \delta)}{\log(1/\delta)}  \le 1$, the PSIPS algorithm satisfies that $\limsup_{\delta \rightarrow 0} \bE_{\bm{\nu}}[\tau_\delta^{\textrm{PS}}] /\log(1/\delta) \leq T^\star(\bm \theta)$ ... both for unstructured PSI ... and transductive linear PSI (bounded convex $\Theta$).

results.notes: This is the expectation of the stopping time in the limit δ → 0. The paper says the result also holds for multivariate Σ-sub-Gaussian distributions, but optimality is reached only in the Gaussian case.

tuning: forced exploration with omega_exp such that V_{omega_exp} is nonsingular

source.label: thm:asymptotic_upper_bound_sample
source.quote: the PSIPS algorithm satisfies that $\limsup_{\delta \rightarrow 0} \bE_{\bm{\nu}}[\tau_\delta^{\textrm{PS}}] /\log(1/\delta) \leq T^\star(\bm \theta)$ for all $\bm{\nu} \in \cD^K$ with regression matrix $\bm \theta \in \Theta$, both for unstructured PSI ... and transductive linear PSI (bounded convex $\Theta$).

results.notes: The paper does not give choices of (c, M) that ensure δ-correctness for general transductive linear PSI, so this is a sample-complexity guarantee only.

conditions: posterior under flat Gaussian prior without inflation

source.label: thm:asymptotic_rate_convergence
source.quote: ... and PSIPS almost surely satisfies that $\liminf_{t \to + \infty} - t^{-1} \log \bP_{\wt \Pi_t \mid \cF_t} ( \Theta \cap \alt(S^\star) ) \ge T^\star(\bm \theta)^{-1} $, both for unstructured PSI ... and transductive linear PSI (bounded convex $\Theta$).

results.notes: This is the exponential decay rate of the posterior probability of misidentifying the Pareto set. The expression is the rate, so the posterior error is roughly exp(-t/T_star).
